sheet-1.description: The lower half of sheet 1 is a map at 100 feet to an inch of the southern end of the borough of Pennington, south of Welling Avenue, which is not itself drawn here. The upper half of the sheet holds the key map of the town at 800 feet to an inch, the water facilities and fire department notes, the title cartouche dated April 1925 and the street and specials index, all outside this part. The map runs from Hale at the upper left across Sked and Burd to South Main at the right. Burd meets Ingleside Avenue, which runs east to South Main and also continues south-west as a diagonal road towards Sked; Vannoy Avenue, marked not open, crosses the foot of the sheet just inside the borough limits, beyond which lies Hopewell Township. The area is thinly built: blocks 47 to 52 are laid out in long narrow lots with scattered frame dwellings and auto houses, many lots still empty. Block 51, east of South Main, is shown only in outline. A fire cistern of 5000 gallons stands at Burd and Ingleside Avenue, and two-inch and six-inch water pipes run along Burd, Ingleside Avenue and South Main. A compass rose at the left gives north straight up the sheet, and a graphic scale of 100 feet to one inch is printed at the lower right. The drawing is sparse, with large areas of bare paper outside the lots along the borough line.
notes: Burd is Burd Street, Sked is Sked Street, Hale is Hale Street and South Main is South Main Street today.
The diagonal Ingleside Avenue south-west of Burd is mapped today as CR 631, which continues as Ingleside Avenue.
Vannoy Avenue is marked not open in 1925.

Top half is the key map (800 ft to an inch), water and fire department notes, title cartouche and street index: not configured. Lower half is a 100 ft map south of Welling Avenue: South Main Street, Burd, Sked, Hale, Ingleside Avenue, Vannoy Avenue (not open). One part (sheet-1).

sheet-2-1.description: The main part of sheet 2 shows the north end of the borough of Pennington at 50 feet to an inch, drawn turned on the page so that North Main runs diagonally from upper left to lower right and north lies about a quarter turn anticlockwise of straight up. It covers North Main from Hansen Place south past East and West Franklin Avenue to Brookside Avenue, and westward to Green Avenue and the double track of the P. and R. Railway along the left edge. Along the railway are the passenger station, a coal trestle, lumber and fertilizer sheds, the Woolsey and Cadwallader coal and lumber yard with its lumber piles, and a cement block works. On Brookside Avenue stands the Pennington Canning Co. with its operating room, storage of canned goods, engine house and water tank. Kintner's Garage stands on North Main at Hansen Place. The rest of the part is residential: frame dwellings with auto houses on deep lots along both Franklin Avenues and North Main, east to the Hopewell Township line, which crosses the upper part of the sheet. Blocks 27, 28, 29, 31, 32 and 54 are numbered, with the key-map numbers in brackets. Water pipes of two to eight inches are drawn in the streets and a fire cistern stands on West Franklin Avenue. The lower right corner, block 31 and 32, is largely open ground; sheet 3 adjoins to the south. A heavy line cuts off an inset at the upper left, which is not part of this description.
notes: Green Avenue south of Brookside Avenue is Green Street today; north of it the modern Green Avenue bends into Railroad Place.
The P. and R. Railway (Philadelphia and Reading) is drawn along the west edge.

50 ft, drawn turned (north about 25 degrees anticlockwise of up). Main part: North Main Street, East and West Franklin Avenues, Brookside Avenue, Green Avenue, Hansen Place, P. and R. Railway with passenger station, Pennington Canning Co., Woolsey and Cadwallader coal and lumber yard. Top-left inset behind a heavy line (own north arrow): North Main Street near the railway freight house and C.A. and T.P. Reed feed mill.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset (top left, behind a heavy line, own north arrow): North Main Street beside the P. and R. Railway with the freight house and C.A. and T.P. Reed feed mill (no street junction; North Main Street and the railway run parallel in the inset; needs parcel corners (locate.py corner) or a carried point; position of the inset on the ground not confirmed).

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 shows the centre of Pennington at 50 feet to an inch with north up. North Main runs down the left third of the sheet to its crossing with West and East Delaware Avenue along the bottom edge; South Main Street is just named below the crossing. Eglantine Avenue runs along the right edge, its east side off the sheet. The blocks on both sides of North Main hold the business centre: a bank at the Delaware Avenue corner, stores, a telephone office, hardware and paint, drug store, an undertaker's shop, Pennington Garage, an auto repair and paint shop, a livery, and the fire department house with a hall, lodge and club above it. Further north the frontage on North Main is residential, with dwellings and auto houses on long lots. Along Eglantine Avenue stand dwellings, two with stone first storeys, and the R.C. Church, with a hatchery and coops in the rear yards of block 32. An iron standpipe and fire cisterns are marked near the crossing, and water pipes of four to eight inches run in the streets. The upper left of the sheet, block 31 north of the stores, and much of block 32 are open lots. Sheets 2, 4 and 5 adjoin to the north, east and south as marked on the margins. A compass rose and a scale of feet are printed at the left.
notes: Only two street junctions are drawn, both on Delaware Avenue; Eglantine Avenue is cut at its centreline by the sheet edge.

50 ft, north up. North Main Street from Delaware Avenue north, West and East Delaware Avenues, Eglantine Avenue; fire department, bank, R.C. church. Only two street junctions (both on Delaware Avenue).

sheet-4-1.description: The main part of sheet 4 lies below the heavy dividing line and shows West Delaware Avenue at 50 feet to an inch with north up, from the railway at the far left past Green Avenue to Hedding at the right. North of Delaware Avenue, west of Green Avenue, block 30 is largely open, with the Philomathean Society Hall and a shed; the tracks of the P. and R. Railway curve across its left corner and a four-inch water pipe runs from the pump and reservoir. East of Green Avenue, block 31 carries a row of dwellings, a blacksmith shop and auto houses facing Delaware Avenue. South of Delaware Avenue lies the campus of Pennington Seminary, a preparatory school for boys: the administration building with the chapel, the main building with west and east wings, kitchen and servants' quarters, steam laundry, carpenter shop, laboratory, infirmary, gymnasium, Junior House, Alpha Omega Hall and a pump house, with a water tank on a tower. The large open ground to the west is marked Athletic Grounds. Hedding runs south along the right edge to sheet 5. Building notes describe the seminary's watchman, heating, lighting and water supply. A compass rose stands on Green Avenue at the dividing line and a scale of feet is printed at the bottom.
notes: Hedding is Burd Street today; Green Avenue south of Brookside Avenue is Green Street.
Pennington Seminary is today The Pennington School.

50 ft, north up, three parts behind heavy lines: part 1 (lower: West Delaware Avenue, Green Avenue, Hedding (Burd), Pennington Seminary, block 31 north of Delaware); part 2 (top left: Franklin Avenue west of Green Avenue, Peerless Insulated Wire and Cable Co.); part 3 (top right: Eglantine Avenue at King Georges Road).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: top left: Franklin Avenue west of Green Avenue, Peerless Insulated Wire and Cable Co. sheet-4-3.description: Part 3 of sheet 4 is the small block at the upper right, above the heavy line and east of Green Avenue, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north up. It shows Eglantine Avenue running north and south through the part, with King Georges Road leaving it eastward at the top edge. West of Eglantine Avenue is the east end of block 32, with four frame dwellings and a shed on lots facing the avenue; east of it is block 33, mostly empty, with the title box of the sheet. An eight-inch water pipe runs in Eglantine Avenue and a four-inch pipe in King Georges Road, with a hydrant at the corner. The south edge of the part is the heavy line marked no exposure, below which sheet 3 continues the blocks along Eglantine Avenue. This part is a northward extension of Eglantine Avenue beyond sheet 3 and is placed from its single street junction only.
notes: King Georges Road is King George Road in OpenStreetMap.
Placed from one hand-picked junction with the atlas scale and the rotation of sheets 3 and 5.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 shows South Main from West and East Delaware Avenue southward to O'Hanlon Avenue at 50 feet to an inch with north up, with Hedding along the left edge. North Main Street is named at the top. West of South Main the blocks between Delaware and Academy Avenue hold stores, the post office and a printing office near Delaware Avenue, then dwellings, the 1st M.E. Church and the large lot of the Public School. East of South Main are the 1st Presbyterian Church with its horse sheds and the Cemetery, then block 36 with dwellings and a dairy. Academy Avenue, also lettered Hedding, crosses the lower part of the sheet; below it Burd and Crawley Avenue run south to O'Hanlon Avenue, with the 1st Baptist Church (colored) between them and dwellings on the narrow lots of blocks 38 and 55. Fire cisterns stand on Delaware Avenue and South Main, and water pipes are drawn in most streets. The right half south of the cemetery is open ground with scattered buildings. Sheets 3, 4 and 6 adjoin as marked on the margins. A compass rose stands at the right and a scale of feet at the lower right.
notes: Hedding is Burd Street today.
Academy Avenue is also lettered Hedding on the sheet.

50 ft, north up. South Main Street from Delaware Avenue to O'Hanlon Avenue, Hedding (Burd), Academy Avenue, Crawley Avenue; public school, 1st Presbyterian church and cemetery, 1st M.E. church, 1st Baptist church (colored).

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 shows the southern residential district of Pennington at 100 feet to an inch with north up, from O'Hanlon Avenue (marked not opened west of Burd) south to West and East Welling Avenue, and from Reading at the left to South Main and the lots east of it. The P. and R. Railway runs along the left edge beside the Hopewell Township line. The cross streets are Laning Avenue, Voorhees Avenue and West and East Curlis Avenue; the north-south streets are Hale, Sked, Burd and South Main. The district is a recent subdivision of long narrow numbered lots (blocks 34 and 37 to 51), most still empty, with scattered frame dwellings and auto houses. Along South Main the lots are denser, with the A.M.E. Church; a school drawn from plans stands in block 46 east of South Main, and a greenhouse with an office stands on Sked in block 42. Fire cisterns of 5000 gallons stand at several corners and water pipes of two to six inches are drawn in the streets. The upper right corner repeats part of sheet 5 (blocks 36 and 38). A compass rose at the left and a scale of 100 feet to one inch at the lower right are printed on the sheet.
notes: Reading is Reading Avenue, Hale is Hale Street, Sked is Sked Street and Burd is Burd Street today.
East Curlis Avenue next to South Main is mapped as Curlis Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
100 ft, north up. O'Hanlon Avenue to Welling Avenue between Reading and South Main Street: Hale, Sked, Burd, Laning, Voorhees, Curlis Avenues; A.M.E. church, school (from plans).
